newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares fall, spooked by foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares fall, spooked by foreign selling.

text.p: Greek shares fell 2.04 percent at the opening on Friday and brokers said the market was unnerved by the absence of further economic improvement and by foreign selling.
"The market has already digested all of the improvement realised in Greece's macroeconomic indicators," said Dimitris Paparistidis, director at Kappa Securities.
"It is waiting for the next bout of good news....(but these) will come later rather than sooner," he added.

On Thursday, provisional Bank of Greece figures for February 1997 showed a widening in Greece's trade balance and current account deficit, coupled with a drop in May forex reserves to $16.3 billion after a brief attack on the drachma.

On the same day, professor Yiannis Spraos, economic advisor to the prime minister submitted a report on economic policy to be pursued in coming years. The report called for tough fiscal and incomes policy measures including a one-off 10 percent tax on corporate profits in 1998.
But National Economy Minister Yiannos Papandoniou made clear the government was not considering adopting such a measure.
"The proposals of professor Spraos are welcome in so far as their aims are anti-inflationary, but the means are not in accordance with the government's pre-defined course," said Paparistidis.
Selling pressure on blue chips and OTE telecom which had provided much support to the index in previous months was affecting the broader market as well.

"Continuing liquidations in blue chips may well be linked to new warrants on Greek instruments, the issuers of which would not favour a swift upward move of the market because they are only partially hedged," said Paparistidis referring to a new call spread warrant on OTE issued by Merrill Lynch.

At current price levels, 6,600 drachmas per share, there is no capital gain in OTE and it is plausible that some big players who ended up with a larger share allotment than initially planned are now reducing their holdings, he added.
The next market-stirring development would be corporate result announcements and bargain-hunting in second-tier stocks.
"The market will be enlivened by announcements of superior interim results in banks and major industrials and greater interest for profitable opportunities away from blue chips," Paparistidis said.
But for the coming month or so, the market will be rather volatile and may drift lower, he added.

"Lacking market-moving news, stocks are expected to consolidate around their current level, while the outlook dor the following days is positive," said Telesis Securities but the market had turned south again.
The Athens general index was 2.49 percent or 38.38 points off at 1,504.87 from Thursday's close of 1,543.25 after 55 minutes of trading.
Turnover amounted to 7.5 billion drachmas on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Decliners beat advancers 141 to 33 with 17 shares unchanged on 191 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $12.25-$12.30. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,113-1,143 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,196-1,256 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998.
Shares of the underlying instrument were unchanged at 6,600 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 512.78-545.51 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $66.87-$68.57. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,016-3,229 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $10.94-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 193-224 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
